name: Museum Grünes Haus
kurzbeschreibung: The Museum Grünes Haus in Reutte: award-winning regional museum in a 16th-century townhouse with art of the Zeiller painters and Via Claudia Augusta.
beschreibung:
Overview

The prestigious Museum Grünes Haus in the market town of Reutte in the Tyrolean Außerfern region is one of the most prominent and architecturally charming regional museums in Tyrol. Housed in a stately 16th-century patrician townhouse on Untermarkt, the building owes its name to the striking green facade painted in 1779. Honoured with the prestigious Austrian Museum Quality Seal, the cultural centre presents exceptional collections showcasing regional history, guild craftsmanship, and distinguished local fine art.

Architecture & Collections

The building itself represents an outstanding historical monument: late-Gothic and Baroque stucco ceilings, artistically panelled Swiss pine parlours (Zirbenstuben), and historic vaults form an authentic backdrop for the permanent exhibits. A highlight of the exterior is the elaborate mural work: renowned Reutte Baroque master Johann Jakob Zeiller (1708–1783) painted the Holy Trinity fresco above the arched entrance portal. The museum dedicates a specialised gallery to the Zeiller family of artists, whose frescoes adorn famous abbeys throughout Austria and southern Germany. Another major focus highlights the ancient Roman military highway Via Claudia Augusta and artifacts excavated from the Roman road station at Katzenberg. In addition, original guild chests, masterpieces, and tools illustrate the golden age of Reutte's painter and stuccoer guilds in the 17th and 18th centuries. Regular temporary exhibitions enrich the cultural programme.

Visit & Arrival

The Museum Grünes Haus is open Tuesday through Saturday from 13:00 to 17:00 (closed on Sundays, Mondays, and public holidays; group tours by prior arrangement). Admission prices (2025/2026 season): Adults €6.00, seniors and students €5.00, children and youths under 18 enjoy free admission! Admission is also free with the regional Aktiv Card of the Naturparkregion Reutte. Arrival by rail: Take the Außerfern Railway (DB/ÖBB) to Reutte in Tirol station; from there it is a five-minute stroll along Untermarkt to the museum (Untermarkt 24). By car: Via the Fernpass road B179 into Reutte; parking is available in the town centre (Untermarkt or Parkdeck Zentrum).

Tips

The historic ground floor featuring the ticket counter and temporary exhibitions offers step-free wheelchair access; upper floors are reached via a heritage staircase. Combine your museum visit with a historic walking tour through Reutte to admire other ornately painted townhouses.
